finding.claim: GET /invoice/<inv_id> returns the full invoice record to unauthenticated callers with no ownership or role check, unlike the sibling /my/invoice/<inv_id> route.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP request to GET /invoice/<inv_id>; inv_id taken from the URL path (invoices.py:8).

trace.note: Route registered with no auth decorator.
inv_id read from the URL path.
INVOICES.get(inv_id) lookup with no caller check; abort(404) only when missing.
Sibling route /my/invoice compares inv['customer'] to g.user['id'], showing the intended ownership check is absent here.

finding.guards_checked: No auth decorator on the route; no before_request hook or middleware in this file setting g.user or rejecting anonymous requests; no owner, tenant, or role comparison before return; no response field filtering. Precondition: attacker knows or can guess an invoice ID (IDs are generated outside this file, so enumerability is unverified). Impact: any invoice's contents, including the customer field, readable without login.

verdict.guard_found: none. invoices.py:7 registers the route with no decorator; invoices.py:9 is a bare dict lookup with abort(404) only on a miss; invoices.py:10 returns the full record. No before_request hook or middleware exists in invoices.py, and it is the only file in the directory. The sibling route at invoices.py:16-17 has the ownership check that this route lacks.
verdict.reason: The route at invoices.py:7-10 returns INVOICES[inv_id] to any anonymous caller with no owner, tenant, or role check, while invoices.py:16-17 shows the intended ownership check on the sibling route. Exploitation requires knowing or guessing an invoice ID, which the code here does not show is hard, and any auth enforced outside this directory (e.g., at a gateway) cannot be seen.
